extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students (mathematics majors or those taking a transition-to-proof course) and their instructors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and learning goals for a first college course that teaches students how to construct, write, and read formal mathematical proofs and to make the transition from computational problem-solving to abstract, proof-oriented mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop logical thinking skills and ability to think more abstractly
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop logical thinking skills and to develop the ability to think more abstractly in a proof oriented setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text frames learning in a proof-oriented environment intended to move students from concrete/calculus problem solving toward abstract mathematical thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct and write mathematical proofs using standard methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop the ability to construct and write mathematical proofs using standard methods of mathematical proof including direct proofs, proof by contradiction, mathematical induction, case analysis, and counterexamples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on mastery of specific proof techniques: direct proof, proof by contradiction, mathematical induction, case analysis, and the use of counterexamples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop the ability to read and understand written mathematical proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop the ability to read and understand written mathematical proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should learn to parse and comprehend the structure and logical flow of others' proofs as part of becoming fluent in mathematical reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop talents for creative thinking and problem solving
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop talents for creative thinking and problem solving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond formal techniques, the course aims to cultivate creativity in constructing proofs and solving nonroutine mathematical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve quality of communication in mathematics (writing, reading, oral)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve their quality of communication in mathematics. This includes improving writing techniques, reading comprehension, and oral communication in mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication skills are treated broadly: clear written proofs, accurate reading/interpretation of mathematical text, and the ability to present mathematics orally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Better understand the nature of mathematics and its language
rubrics_metrics.description: Better understand the nature of mathematics and its language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should gain insight into what mathematics is, how mathematical statements are formed, and the conventions of mathematical notation and discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for upper-level, proof-based mathematics courses (transition goal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide students with material that will be needed for their further study of mathematics; serve as a 'transition course' from the calculus sequence to upper-level courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course is intended to bridge from problem-solving-focused calculus to abstract/theoretical courses; students are expected to be able to read and construct coherent, understandable proofs and should have a background of one semester of calculus.
